description: Inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference. The jīva is simultaneously one with and different from Bhagavān. Neither monism nor dualism.
Relationship — the jīva's eternal constitutional position as servant of Kṛṣṇa. First of the three categories of Gauḍīya theology.
Process — bhakti-yoga as the means of reawakening the dormant relationship. Second category.
Goal — prema (pure love of Godhead). The ultimate aim of all spiritual practice. Third category.
Kṛṣṇa as the original Supreme Person from whom all avatāras emanate. The source of all sources.
Transformation of energy — the world is real transformation of the Lord's energy not illusion. Distinguishes Gauḍīya from Advaita.
The individual soul — eternal marginal energy (taṭasthā-śakti) of the Lord. Qualitatively one quantitatively different.
External energy — the covering and throwing potency that obscures the jīva's constitutional position.
Devotional service — the intrinsic function (svarūpa-śakti) of the jīva. Nine processes beginning with śravaṇam.
The Holy Name — non-different from Kṛṣṇa. Primary practice in Kali-yuga. Harinām-saṅkīrtana.
Transcendental mellow — five primary: śānta dāsya sakhya vātsalya mādhurya. The science of divine relationship.
The spiritual master — representative of Kṛṣṇa transparent medium of the paramparā. Essential for transmission.
Divine pastimes — eternally manifest in the spiritual world. Not allegory not mythology — ontological reality.
The divine abode — Goloka Vṛndāvana as the highest realm. Non-different from Kṛṣṇa's own form.
Time — an energy of the Lord. Governs creation maintenance dissolution. Manifests as yuga cycle.
